items.title: The full pair and its shorter shapes

states.label: The full pair
states.sm: Ona alu lea ʻo le tama.
states.note: *Ona* opens the clause and *lea* closes the verb phrase.

states.label: Without *lea*
states.note: Without *lea*, the named participant stands in its plain form.

states.label: Without *ona*
states.note: *Lea* carries the succession, and the participant usually has the presenting particle.

items.caption: These are next-event examples from a story: a text needs something before them. Modern writing keeps the full pair; speech also uses the shorter shapes.

items.title: Which parts of the pair remain?

prompts.sm: Ona alu loa lea ʻo le tama.
prompts.why: Both *ona* and *lea* remain. The extra *loa* is the then-word inside the verb phrase.
*Ona* carries the succession on its own, and *lea* is absent.

prompts.sm: Alu loa lea ʻo le tama.
prompts.why: *Ona* is absent. The then-word *loa* and the closing word *lea* remain.

items.intro: Find the opening and closing words, without treating the extra then-word as part of the pair.
